activity.title: I’m excited to announce that I’ll be taking my talents to Cisco this summer as a Software Engineering Intern in San Jose! I’m incredibly grateful to my family and friends for their constant encouragement, as well as the Cisco recruiting team for their guidance and support throughout this entire process. I’m looking forward to contributing to impactful software initiatives and learning from an exceptional team. If you’ll be in the San Jose area this summer, I’d love to connect!

As my time at PNC Bank comes to an end, I am truly grateful for the opportunity I had to work with the Enterprise AI Technology team over the last ten weeks. Throughout the summer, I worked at the intersection of product and enterprise AI, building agentic workflows, driving cross-functional adoption to hundreds of active users, and defining requirements to build, own, and deliver an end-to-end AI support platform for the Copilot Center of Excellence. A special thank you to my manager, Em Frank , along with Fred Caicedo , Valerie Groskreutz , and Christopher K. . I am super appreciative of the opportunity, the guidance, and the challenge to keep improving day in, day out. To Anurag Palakurti , thank you for being a great teammate and friend, and thank you to all of my fellow interns and mentors who made this summer so memorable! Looking forward to the fall, I’m excited to announce that I’ll be joining Tesla , supporting their Global Supply Management Team for Optimus and Drive Systems! I’m extremely excited to dive into this experience and look forward to learning from the team. A huge thank you to Amishi Chokshi for the smooth recruiting process and Daniel Vitale for the opportunity. Excited for what’s to come! ⚡️

This past Friday, I officially wrapped up my summer as a Software Engineering Intern on Cisco's Industrial IoT team in San Jose! Over the past few months, I worked on Agentic Runbook Creator (ARC) for Cisco's AI Assistant for Troubleshooting Networks. Runbooks are step-by-step diagnostic scripts used to troubleshoot industrial networks automatically, and ARC is used to generate said runbooks dynamically using context from a customer's network. My work included connecting local SLM-based hypothesis generation with cloud LLM workflows and protecting sensitive topology and device data during the handoff between on-premises and cloud activity. I also directly developed a cloud-based digital-twin evaluator that injects IOS-XE simulated faults into the customer's obfuscated topology to test whether the generated runbooks actually work. Ultimately, we brought estimated network downtime for new faults from hours to ~25 minutes, and expanded runbook coverage beyond 13 preexisting implementations! Working on ARC gave me a much better understanding of what it takes to build AI for real systems. The output needs the right context, and the workflow has to protect customer data from the start. The whole system also needs to hold up when tested against realistic failures. Taking the project from separate components to a connected workflow taught me a lot about integration and iteration, while working on an engineering team showed me how much I can learn from asking questions and listening to feedback. I'm heading back to UIUC soon, excited to keep building on these skills and apply them in future projects. I want to thank Nikhil Mathur , my mentor, and Dhananjay Awaji , my manager, for all their guidance and support throughout the summer. I'm also grateful to Elango Ganesan , Distinguished Engineer at Cisco, for taking the time to review ARC and give us invaluable feedback that helped move the project forward. Furthermore, I would like to thank Judy Heng, Alexandra Cortes , & Robin J Gonsalves (Robbie Gonsalves) for organizing events and providing amazing intern experiences. Thank you to Pranav Butaney & Srivishnu Vusirikala , my fellow intern teammates who worked alongside me on ARC. Finally, thank you to Abhishek Prabhu , Nitish G. , Nidhi Prakash , Jasraj Sidhu , & Adam Boswell , for making this summer so fun and memorable. Working at Cisco gave me stronger confidence in my abilities and a lot of great memories! #WeAreCisco #Intern

You are already in the top 1% of AI users. There is a gap between you and the people running twenty terminals at once. You are never closing it, and you do not need to. Now turn around. The median employee at your company has opened ChatGPT maybe four times in two years. They tried it on an old model, decided it was stupid, and never came back. Every AI strategy deck I read assumes that person eventually catches up. They will not. Every rollout I have seen splits the same way, whether it is fifty people or five thousand. Five to ten percent become power users. Twenty percent use it badly. Seventy percent never touch it. One executive I spoke with had committed ten million dollars a year to licenses. Ten percent of the org burns ninety percent of the tokens. If everyone were genuinely good at this the bill would be a hundred million. Their best case is their worst case. Meanwhile the dashboard says adopted. McKinsey has 78% of organisations using AI and more than 80% of those reporting no impact on earnings. Both are honest. Adoption is binary, skill is a spectrum, and your tracker only measures the binary. Train your top slice and give them somewhere to publish. For everyone else, put the AI in the background of the systems they already work in. What is your organisation actually measuring? Read the full blog post here: https://lnkd.in/gqUkKBsj
